interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis following radical prostatectomy is influenced by several documented factors. Favorable findings include a negative surgical margin (0.0) and no invasion of the seminal vesicles (0.0). The Gleason pattern was 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3), and there was no extraprostatic extension. Countervailing factors include the preoperative PSA of 18 and the absence of lymph node removal, as nodal status is documented as 'no nodes removed,' which widens uncertainty as pNx is not equivalent to pN0. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy difference is noted as the Gleason pattern and ISUP report are missing. The primary uncertainty lies in the postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory, as this information is currently absent. Missing nodal sampling further complicates the assessment of local control. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and their trend is crucial for revising this prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 55.71 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 36.21–75.22 months; its coverage has not been validated.
